title: LicoUp deployment facts
description: What one installation actually has, as the host publishes it: the profile it was installed from, each known package's four independent facts, and the availability of each capability. Available, installed, enabled and active are separate on purpose — there is no single `ready`, and a local import is installed without ever having been in a directory.

profile.description: The recipe this installation started from. A profile is an initial selection, not a permanent prohibition: the user may change it or add packages at any time. The workflow and flywheel are kernel capabilities, so no profile selects them.

corePackage.description: The minimal trusted host: canonical conversation, the Assistant, the workflow and flywheel, the extension host with package management, the base usage journal, the declarative interface primitives, the generic PTY/CLI adapter with Agent Hub configuration registration, key custody, and update and migration admission. Its capabilities cannot be trimmed away, and it may not require a package that can.

source.description: Where it came from. A local import needs no directory and no account, and being unpublished is not being illegal.

available.description: Present in a directory. `installed` does not imply this.

enabled.description: Installed and not disabled. Enabled is not started: activation stays lazy.

active.description: An instance of this package is running.

lifecycle.description: `verified` (a publisher signature was checked) and `local-approved` (the user bound trust to specific content) are two different trust facts, and neither is more installed than the other.

instanceLifecycles.description: One package version may produce several instances with different permissions. Their states are separate from the package's.

declinedOptional.description: Optional dependencies that were declared and deliberately not installed. Reported so the user can decide; never resolved silently.

owner.description: The package that must be present for this capability to work at all. One capability may be offered by several packages; this names the one the default distribution provides.

core.description: True when the kernel carries it, so every distribution has it.

availability.description: Every value other than `served` is a legal configuration and a catalogue fact. An operation that needs an unavailable capability is refused as an unavailable capability, never as a malformed request.
